notes.title: v2.1.0.0 Patch
notes.notes:
This is just a small patch that adds mouse support. If you guys run into any issues with using the mouse don't hesitate to let me know in the Support discussions!

Note: The tutorial is still based on keyboard controls, since I'm still regarding that as the native control scheme.

[Edit]
I should probably clarify how the mouse can be used:
- All menu options (except the Infobank) can be selected via left-clicking the mouse (clicking outside a menu will close it)
- Your character will now face towards the cursor (when the cursor is moving)
- Holding right-click will make your character move in whatever direction it's facing, and can also cancel any current action taking place
- The left-click is an alternative "Interact" button, so holding it down while the character is facing a patch of grass will bring up the Build Menu, or make him/her start chopping down a tree, etc

A more important note: detecting whether the cursor is within the boundaries of a button seems a little off when the game is running in Windowed mode, but works perfect when in fullscreen.

notes.title: v2.0.0.0 Patch
notes.notes:
So here it is... the big 2.0 with the last major [planned] feature: raids on the village. Does this mean I will no longer be developing/updating/supporting the game? Absolutely not. If bugs are reported, they will still be getting fixed asap... and there's a few minor requests people have made (i.e. mouse integration) that I'll still be working on.

Changes and Fixes:
- Added 'Raid' events where monsters emerge from the cave and attack your village (they chase down you and your villagers... whatever's closest)
- Implemented combat between NPCs
- Made the sound location-based, so the further away a sound is taking place the quieter it will be (max of 20 tiles away)
- Added villagers dying of starvation to the "Normal" difficulty
- Gave "Hardcore" difficulty permadeath (your current save and/or autosave gets deleted if you die)
- Decreased the delay between combat turns
- Allowed NPCs to also take advantage of the speed increase from roads/bridges
- Probably other tweaks/fixes that I can't remember at the moment :P

Note: if your current save is with the "Hardcore" difficulty and you don't wish to risk losing it, you can open the save file with any text editor (i.e. Notepad) and simply change 'Difficulty="Hardcore"' at the very top to 'Difficulty="Normal"'.

notes.title: v1.8.8.7 Patch
notes.notes:
Changes and Fixes:
- Fixed a bug where being in the middle of an action and having it interrupted by a wolf attack does not fully cancel the action
- Fixed a bug where changing equipment could cause more than one thing to be considered 'equipped' when there's more than one of it with the same name
- Made the weapons/armor equipped by other characters not display in the currently opened inventory... so if you're changing the weapon of a villager, no other villager's weapon (or the player's weapon) will be displayed
- Fixed a bug with being able to place Torch decorations when there are no torches stored in the village inventory
- Made crafting a Torch automatically store it in the village inventory
- Decreased the rate at which NPCs 'wander' to make it a little easier to interact with villagers and the Mentor
- Fixed a bug with decorations not getting built
- Fixed a bug with the Torch highlight preview displaying when going to craft a Torch (it's only supposed to display when going to place one as a 'decoration')
- Added a cap of Max Population * 2 to the amount of items that can be passively generated in the village inventory by jobs (this doesn't affect manually transferring items)
- Changed the order in which the village events happen each in-game hour, so that now: 1) Villagers eat the food, 2) Resources get replenished by jobs, 3) Chance of getting new villagers is calculated, 4) Villagers (if any) get recruited
- Cut the resource costs of all the armor by half
- Reduced the cost of Leather to 2 Fur

notes.title: v1.7.3.0 Patch
notes.notes:
This is a patch to make mod content overwrite existing content (not the Core files themselves, but everything created from them), which I felt was something really missing from the modding side of the game. Previously, in order to do something like make the main character start with different armor, you had to edit the Core file itself. It's not really a big deal to have to edit the Core file... but what if there were 5 different mods all changing different properties of the main character? Well, this patch makes it so 5 different mods can do exactly that.

Note: If mods are trying to overwrite the same properties of the same objects, then whatever is loaded last will 'win' (they load in alphabetical order).

notes.title: v1.6.4 Hotfix
notes.notes:
Fixes and Changes:
- Fixed a major bug with the loading of items stored in the village inventory (what was causing everyone's game to crash when loading a save). No clue how such a game breaking bug has gone undetected/unreported for so long... but it's fixed now :D Thanks to everyone who emailed me their save files to track it down!
- Overhauled the options menu

Known bugs that I'm (still) investigating: 
- Attempting to loot a chest in the dungeon can either refuse to transfer its loot or outright crash the game
- There was a report that opening the player inventory crashed the game (?)

What I'm currently working on:
- Implementing being able to change resolutions. When investigating the major bug mentioned above, I noticed that things were being drawn to the screen in really off places due to the games having been saved with different resolutions. It's not a problem for someone saving/loading a game on a comp where the resolution is never changing, but it's a problem when loading the save anywhere else. Anyways, it's proving tricky getting everything to re-align correctly after switching to a different resolution in-game >.<

Just a quick patch that adds a button to the Options Menu for switching between a Fullscreen Borderless Window (default) and just plain Windowed.

Some of you may be wondering why there's no options for changing the resolution? Well, I was crafty and made all the graphics/text scale to whatever your desktop resolution is... soooo (in theory) there should never be a need to change the resolution. It should simply look the same on all of them (from 800x600 to 153,600x86,400). Seriously, though, if you guys find a resolution where things look particularly 'wrong', please let me know!
